Generalized Fluctuation Test (GFT), scale-aware re-implementation

Source: R/hcp_gft.R
hcp_gft.Rd

Structural change detection by multiple breaks in a linear model. This is a native re-implementation (no strucchange dependency) and an adaptation of the original strucchange::breakpoints approach with documented innovations: (1) the least-squares (mean-only) Bai & Perron breakpoints are generalised to a Gaussian mean + variance segmentation cost (each segment pays the ML deviance m * log(RSS/m) with a per-segment variance), so breaks in scale/variance regimes are detected, not only breaks in the mean/trend; (2) the number of breaks is chosen by the conservative LWZ information criterion (Liu, Wu & Zidek 1997) instead of the Gaussian BIC, which curbs over-segmentation; (3) the Bai-Perron dynamic program is vectorised.

This mirrors the canonical implementation in the pyharbinger package (class HcpGft); the two implementations produce identical detections.

Usage

hcp_gft(penalty = "lwz")

Arguments

penalty

break-count information criterion: "lwz" (default, conservative) or "bic".

Value

hcp_gft object

References

  • Bai J, Perron P (1998). Estimating and testing linear models with multiple structural changes. Econometrica, 66(1):47-78.

  • Bai J, Perron P (2003). Computation and analysis of multiple structural change models. Journal of Applied Econometrics, 18(1):1-22.

  • Liu J, Wu S, Zidek JV (1997). On segmented multivariate regression. Statistica Sinica, 7:497-525. (LWZ information criterion)

  • Chen J, Gupta AK (2000). Parametric Statistical Change Point Analysis. Birkhauser. (Gaussian mean+variance change points)

  • Killick R, Fearnhead P, Eckley IA (2012). Optimal detection of changepoints with a linear computational cost. JASA, 107(500):1590-1598.

  • Zeileis A, Leisch F, Kleiber C, Hornik K (2002). strucchange: An R package for testing for structural change in linear regression models. Journal of Statistical Software, 7(2). doi:10.18637/jss.v007.i02 (original approach)

Examples

library(daltoolbox)

# Load change-point example data
data(examples_changepoints)

# Use a simple example
dataset <- examples_changepoints$simple
head(dataset)
#>   serie event
#> 1  0.00 FALSE
#> 2  0.25 FALSE
#> 3  0.50 FALSE
#> 4  0.75 FALSE
#> 5  1.00 FALSE
#> 6  1.25 FALSE

# Configure the GFT detector
model <- hcp_gft()

# Fit the detector (no-op for GFT)
model <- fit(model, dataset$serie)

# Run detection
detection <- detect(model, dataset$serie)

# Show detected change points
print(detection[(detection$event),])
#>    idx event        type
#> 49  49  TRUE changepoint
